question: The bacteria conducting an anoxygenic photosynthesis use which of the following compounds as an electron donor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen sulphide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis is a type of photosynthesis performed by certain bacteria where oxygen is not released as a by-product.
 
• Bacteria conducting anoxygenic photosynthesis use hydrogen sulphide (H2S) as an electron donor instead of water.
 
• During this process, hydrogen sulphide is oxidized to produce elemental sulfur (S) or sulfate (SO4²⁻) as a by-product.
 
• These bacteria possess specialized pigments like bacteriochlorophylls to absorb light energy and drive photosynthesis in anaerobic environments.
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis typically occurs in environments with low oxygen levels, such as deep-sea sediments, hot springs, or sulfur-rich regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose:**

 
 
• Glucose is an organic compound and a primary energy source for most living organisms.
 
• It is utilized during cellular respiration but is not used as an electron donor in photosynthesis.
 
• In oxygenic photosynthesis, glucose is synthesized as a product of the Calvin Cycle.
 
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide:**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a key reactant in photosynthesis, used in the Calvin Cycle to form glucose.
 
• It is not an electron donor but acts as a carbon source for both oxygenic and anoxygenic photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Water:**
 
 
• Water (H₂O) is used as an electron donor in oxygenic photosynthesis by plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
• It undergoes photolysis, releasing oxygen (O₂) as a by-product.
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis, however, does not use water as an electron donor.
 
 
 
• **Anoxygenic Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This process is carried out by bacteria like purple sulfur bacteria, green sulfur bacteria, and heliobacteria.
 
• Electron donors include hydrogen sulphide, ferrous iron, or organic compounds, depending on the environment and bacterial species.
 
• It plays a crucial role in sulfur and nutrient cycling in anaerobic ecosystems.
